text: Stop there. Don't come near the edge — the boards are rotten, and the water's deeper than it looks. Like everything in this Mire.
A lamplighter… Fancy that. I thought your kind were gone. Thought I was the last one left who remembered what light is for.

choices.text: I need to get to the islet. To the beacon.
What are those lights over the bog?

wisps.text: Marsh gas. Burns pretty, warm — from afar just like a beacon. People walked toward that fire and never came back. It promises nothing, it just burns and waits for you to stumble. Remember: true light doesn't run away when you walk toward it.

text: To the beacon, then. You can't walk across the channel — it's deep as a well there. Only by boat.
And the boat leaks. Twenty years I've ferried no one — she's dried out. Same as me.

choices.text: Take me anyway, I'll pay with oil.

oil.text: Keep your oil — you need it more. Here we take payment in deeds, not oil. That's how it was under my father and that's how it'll be under me, while I breathe.

ask.text: Bring me rope — on the old boardwalk, to the west, I dropped a coil somewhere. I'll unpick it for caulking. And resin — it's on the dead tree by the tussocks to the north. Only don't go toward the light itself. Walk the tussocks and look at your feet, not at the glow.

waiting.text: Rope's on the western boardwalk. Resin's on the dead tree to the north, by the tussocks. The boat will wait. She and I both know how to wait.

alt.text: You found the rope, good. Now the resin — on the dead tree to the north, by the tussocks. And don't follow the light, you hear?

text: Let's see… Good rope. And the resin — smells right, of the woods and of patience.
Sit a while, I'll be quick. Caulking is simple work: tight, along the seam, no hurry. Like everything that holds water.

choices.text: Why did you stay here alone?

why.text: Someone has to remember where the channel is. If I leave, there won't be a trace. I'm not waiting for the light to come back, lamplighter. I'm waiting for people to come back. It's not the same thing, though it looks alike.

fixed.text: Done. She holds. Get in when you're ready — at the pier. And here, take my ferry book. There's something written in it I've kept quiet about. Twenty years. That's enough.

ready.text: The boat is ready. Say the word at the pier — I'll take you.

text: Hear that? Frogs. Shouting like they've been kept out of the choir for twenty years. The water's babbling — I'd forgotten it knew how to babble and not just stand.
You know, I think I'll paint the boat. Red. So it can be seen from the shore — the ferry's running. Let them come.
And you — go to the mountains, west, past the village. Old Ansar is there with his observatory. He knows more about the smoke than anyone. Only dress warm — up there the cold eats fire.
What's this? Bread… Still warm. Who's it from?
…From Mara. Twenty years. For twenty years I thought the Ford had forgotten me. And it turns out they were waiting. It was I who forgot the road.
Take this oil. I kept a store for a dark day. And look — the day turned out bright.
